newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japanese hostages urge quick end to siege - Kyodo.
newsitem.headline: Japanese hostages urge quick end to siege - Kyodo.

text.p: Japanese still held captive in the Lima hostage siege on Sunday urged a quick end to the standoff because their situation was becoming more dangerous, Kyodo news agency reported.

Kyodo said that in a letter to Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto carried out by nine Japanese hostages released earlier on Sunday, the still captive Japanese, numbering about 20 diplomats and businessmen, said they wanted to be freed as quickly as possible.
A foreign ministry spokesman had no comment on the report.

"If this bad precedent is left as it is, it could have a serious effect on the future economic activities of both Peru and Japan, and we are anxious to see it resolved as early as possible," Kyodo quoted the letter as saying.

The Japanese are the biggest group of non-Peruvians held by about 20 members of the Marxist Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement who took over the Japanese ambassador's residence on December 17 during a party to celebrate Japanese Emperor Akihito's 63rd birthday.

While acknowledging their captors were treating them properly, the letter said:"But if the situation in which heavily armed soldiers keep a close watch on us lasts for a long time, it will become extremely difficult for us to keep the balance between mind and body."

"This situation is getting more dangerous day by day," the letter added. "We ask you (Prime Minister Hashimoto) to make a stronger request to the Peruvian government urgently to set free all the Japanese held as hostages at an early date."
